question: The price of fuel decreases by 40%, 25% and 45% in three successive months, but increases by 55% in the fourth month. What is the percentage increase/decrease in the price of fuel in the fourth month as compared to its original price? (Round off your answer to two decimal places)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Take initial price = 100

After 40% decrease ⇒ 60

After 25% decrease ⇒ 60 × 0.75 = 45

After 45% decrease ⇒ 45 × 0.55 = 24.75

**∴ After 55% increase ⇒ 24.75 × 1.55 = 38.36 ⇒ decrease = 61.64%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Successive changes: −40%, −25%, −45%, +55%

**Formula used:**

New value = Original × successive multipliers

**Calculation:**

⇒ Assume initial price = 100

⇒ After 40% decrease: 100 × 0.60 = 60

⇒ After 25% decrease: 60 × 0.75 = 45

⇒ After 45% decrease: 45 × 0.55 = 24.75

⇒ After 55% increase: 24.75 × 1.55 = 38.3625

⇒ Net change = 38.3625 − 100 = −61.6375

⇒ Percentage change = −61.64%

**∴ The price decreases by 61.64%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage

Use multipliers: (1 ± rate/100) for each step

Net Effect

Final value compared with original gives overall % change

Base Method

Assume initial value = 100 for easier calculation
